description: Objective of the course is to make students understand the concepts of game theory and its applications to various engineering disciplines.

syllabus.title: Introduction and Outline
syllabus.body: Definitions, utilities, rationality, intelligence, common knowledge, classification of games and real-world scenarios.

syllabus.title: Non-Cooperative Game Theory
syllabus.body: Extensive and strategic form games, dominant strategy equilibria, pure and mixed strategy Nash equilibrium with key results such as the Nash theorem, computation of Nash equilibria, matrix games: saddle points, minimax theorem, Bayesian games and Bayesian Nash equilibrium, evolutionary game theory (ESS strategies), repeated games.

syllabus.title: Mechanism Design
syllabus.body: The mechanism design environment, social choice functions, implementation of social choice functions, incentive compatibility and revelation theorem, Gibbard-Satterthwaite and Arrow impossibility theorem, Vickrey-Clarke-Groves (VCG) mechanisms, Bayesian mechanisms, revenue equivalence theorem, Myerson optimal auction.

syllabus.title: Cooperative Game Theory
syllabus.body: Correlated strategies and correlated equilibrium, the Nash bargaining problem, coalitional games (transferable utility games), the core, the Shapley value, other solution concepts: kernel, nucleolus.

outcomes: To understand the concepts of game theory and its mathematical foundation.
To identify fields of application of game theory in real-life.
To design and implement game theoretic algorithms for automation.
To apply game theoretic strategies in industrial engineering problems.
textbooks: Martin J. Osborne, An Introduction to Game Theory, Oxford University Press, Indian Edition, 2003.
Roger B. Myerson, Game Theory: Analysis of Conflict, Harvard University Press, 1991.
